hook: Inducing torpor in rats cut heart injury by about 40% in isolated hearts after blocked blood flow.

readout.label: Infarct size reduction, ex vivo rat heart

summary: Chemogenetic activation of a hypothalamic region put rats, which never enter torpor naturally, into a torpor-like state. Their hearts were then tested ex vivo with simulated heart attack injury, and infarct size fell by about 40%, even when the animal had not become cold. Phosphoproteomics suggested more survival signaling and less cell-death signaling. Protection was shown only in isolated hearts, not in living animals.
title: Synthetic torpor in the rat protects the heart from ischaemia-reperfusion injury.
